Salisbury QLD, Full Time, Trades & Services
Vacancy Listing Dates 27/07/2026 to 24/08/2026
Please Quote Reference Number 17825
- Skilled Light Vehicle Mechanic required
- Full time opportunity
- Join the team at Autoworks Pty Ltd

Autoworks Pty Ltd are a busy, independent mechanical workshop specialising in the servicing, maintenance, diagnostics, and repair of a wide range of light vehicles. The workshop offers varied and challenging work in a practical, fast-paced environment where quality workmanship, teamwork, and customer satisfaction are highly valued. It is well suited to someone who enjoys problem-solving, takes pride in their work, and is committed to delivering high-quality mechanical services.

We are seeking a qualified and experienced Light Vehicle Mechanic with strong skills in diagnostics, fault-finding, servicing, and mechanical repairs.

The ideal candidate will have experience working on a wide range of light vehicles and be confident using diagnostic equipment to identify and resolve faults. They should be reliable, detail-oriented, and able to work independently while maintaining high standards of workmanship and safety. Strong communication skills, a positive attitude, and a commitment to delivering quality service are essential.

Your role will include, but is not limited to:
- Diagnose and identify mechanical, electrical and electronic faults in light vehicles using specialised diagnostic equipment and manufacturer specifications to determine appropriate repair solutions.
- Perform scheduled servicing, logbook maintenance and preventative maintenance on a wide range of passenger, performance, classic and modified vehicles in accordance with manufacturer recommendations.
- Repair or replace worn, damaged or defective mechanical components including engine parts, clutches, gearboxes,
differentials, braking components, suspension assemblies, steering systems, cooling systems and exhaust systems.
- Inspect, dismantle, repair and reassemble engines, transmissions, steering, suspension, braking, cooling and driveline systems, ensuring all components meet manufacturer and workshop quality standards.
- Conduct engine diagnostics, electronic fuel injection (EFI) repairs, engine management system testing and fault rectification using computer-based diagnostic equipment.
- Carry out engine overhauls, engine conversions and other mechanical upgrades for light vehicles, ensuring all work is completed safely and in accordance with engineering and workshop specifications.
- Install and integrate performance components and aftermarket mechanical systems, including turbochargers, suspension upgrades and associated vehicle modifications while maintaining vehicle reliability and safety.
- Test, adjust and inspect repaired or serviced vehicles through workshop testing and road testing to verify performance, drivability and compliance with operational and safety requirements.
- Assist with custom vehicle builds by carrying out mechanical installation, fitting and assembly work in collaboration with fabrication and auto electrical teams.
- Inspect vehicles for mechanical condition, identify repair requirements, provide accurate recommendations for additional maintenance where necessary, and maintain detailed service records in accordance with workshop procedures and regulatory requirements.

Applicants must have:
- Relevant trade qualification AQF Certificate IV with at least one year of relevant experience. Alternatively, at least three years of full-time relevant experience in lieu of a formal qualification.
- Strong diagnostic and fault-finding skills using modern diagnostic equipment.
- Effective communication skills and the ability to work independently or as part of a team.

In joining us, you'll benefit from long-term, stable employment with opportunities to develop advanced skills in diagnostics, automotive electrical systems, engine conversions, and vehicle modifications. The role offers varied and challenging work, ongoing training, and the potential to progress into a Senior Technician or Workshop Leadership position.

A salary of $79,000 - $95,000 will be offered to the successful candidate.

Apply now through our online application form -
https://www.netyourjob.com.au/jobs/17825.php

Location: Airport West, VIC 3042
Full-Time: Immediate start
Reports to: Floor Manager
Job Title: Fitter
Salary range: $79,500 - $85,000 + Superannuation – depending on skill level.
Job Closure date:3 0 days

About our client:
Our client, a renowned leader in the automotive repair industry with over three decades of excellence, is seeking a dedicated and meticulous Fitter to join their dynamic team. Renowned for their commitment to precision and restoring vehicles to their pre-accident condition, they operate from a state-of-the-art facility. If you have a passion for automotive craftsmanship and a keen eye for detail, this is your opportunity to contribute to a business that sets the industry standard.

About the Role:
In this pivotal role, you will be responsible for the hands-on structural and panel fitting that forms the foundation of every vehicle restoration. You will work on a variety of vehicles, utilizing advanced equipment and techniques to ensure every repair meets rigorous safety and quality standards. This position is perfect for a technician who takes pride in their work and understands that a perfect fit is the first step to a flawless finish.

Key Duties & Responsibilities:
Vehicle Structure & Frame Analysis:
• Conduct comprehensive inspections of vehicle collision damage to assess structural integrity and identify misalignments in frames, unibody structures, and suspension mounting points.
• Utilize advanced frame straightening equipment and hydraulic systems to meticulously pull and correct structural damage back to the manufacturer’s original specifications.
• Diagnose and perform precise repairs on a vehicle's underlying structure, ensuring its safety and performance are fully restored.

Precision Panel Fitting & Alignment:
• Expertly install, align, and fit a wide range of metal panels, frames, and subassemblies—including doors, fenders, quarter panels, and bumpers—to achieve perfect contours and structural integrity.
• Meticulously adjust all replacement parts to ensure consistent, manufacturer-specified gaps and flushness across the entire vehicle body.
• Modify or custom-fabricate replacement body panels through skilled cutting, grinding, bending, and welding of sheet metal to perfectly match the vehicle's original contours.

Technical Interpretation & Mechanical Fitting:
• Interpret complex technical specifications, detailed vehicle blueprints, and comprehensive collision repair guides to determine the correct materials, tools, and sequences for each unique repair task.
• Perform the fitting and installation of mechanical components such as exhaust systems, fuel lines, and associated brackets, ensuring all parts are securely mounted and functionally sound.

Quality Control & Surface Preparation:
• Employ precision measuring instruments including callipers, micrometres, and specialised alignment tools to verify the accuracy of gaps, contours, and dimensions on all repaired or replaced body parts.
• Prepare vehicle surfaces for refinishing by undertaking skilled sanding, application of body fillers, and priming to create a perfectly smooth substrate, ready for painting.
Equipment Operation & Maintenance:
• Configure and operate a range of specialised workshop machinery, including MIG/MAG welding equipment, frame straighteners, and pneumatic/hydraulic tools, tailoring their settings for specific repair applications.

The Ideal Candidate Will Have:
• A proven track record as a Vehicle Fitter, Panel Beater, or in a similar role within the automotive repair industry.
• Formal qualifications in Automotive Body Repair, Metal Fabrication, or a related trade are highly regarded.
• Proficiency in reading and interpreting technical drawings and repair procedures.
• Demonstrated, hands-on experience with welding, metal fabrication, and the use of precision measuring tools.
• Strong mechanical aptitude and a meticulous approach to every task, with an unwavering commitment to quality.
• The ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a cohesive team in a fast-paced environment.
• A strong commitment to adhering to all workplace health and safety guidelines.

If you are a skilled Fitter ready to take on a rewarding role with a company that values quality and expertise, we encourage you to apply.

Please note: We are acting as recruitment agents on behalf of our client. Employer details will be provided to shortlisted candidates.

result.description:
Bioproperties Pty Ltd 
Glenorie, Sydney NSW 2157

Full Time Life Scientist 
$80,000 p.a.

Summary
The Life Scientist is responsible for gathering scientific data, designing experiments, and executing upstream and downstream manufacturing processes for microbiological vaccines. 
The position involves interaction with Research and Development partners to ensure the scientific content and approach in R&D experiments meet suitable GMP and GLP standards, guaranteeing a timely outcome for the Company. The ideal candidate combines meticulous execution with strict adherence to biosecurity, quality assurance, and Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP). 

Key Responsibilities
•	Design and conduct complex experiments, record precise observations/measurements, analyse biological data, and prepare or supervise the preparation of laboratory reports. 
•	Ensure the environmental conditions for each of the current vaccine products are suitable for maximum multiplication to maximise the efficacy of the resulting live veterinary vaccine. 
•	Provide scientific knowledge and biotechnological input to new potential products in research and development phases to ensure efficient transfer and scale up to manufacturing. 
•	Support laboratory scientists in the research, development, and scale-up of biotechnological processes, including assisting in the design of Development Record Sheets. 
•	Review and analyse data to make meaningful conclusions and outcomes, presenting data and trial results to BPL Management and R&D teams. 
•	Inoculate, propagate, and harvest live microbiological strains used in vaccine production. 
•	Perform aseptic techniques and sterile manipulations within cleanroom environments. 
•	Carry out cleanroom setup prior to production and perform line clearance after production activities. 
•	Perform decontamination of production waste using validated autoclave systems. 
•	Prepare, package, and handle biological materials including vials and bottles for sterilisation. 
•	Critically review completed general production/laboratory documentation (production batch records, environmental monitoring records) for the operation of biotechnology equipment with a strict emphasis on product quality standards and GMP compliance. 
•	Write and/or review Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Production Record Sheets (PRSs), and other controlled documents as required. 
•	Ensure compliance with biosecurity regulations and applicable regulatory requirements. 
•	Perform Risk Assessments, Corrective and Preventative (CAPA) investigations, raise Deviation/Incident Reports (DIR), and initiate Change Controls (CC) when necessary, including root cause analysis in biotechnology deviations. 
•	Support documentation control for viral, bacterial, and mycoplasma strains. 

Qualification & Experience
•	Bachelor's or Master's degree in Life Science, Biotechnology, Microbiology, or a highly related discipline. 
•	At least 1+ years of relevant industry experience in life sciences or pharmaceutical GMP quality vaccine manufacturing.  
•	Experience working in a laboratory or biopharmaceutical manufacturing environment. 
•	Exposure to microbial culture handling. 
•	Familiarity with GMP standards, documentation practices, and quality assurance control systems. 
•	High attention to detail with strong commitment to quality and compliance.
•	Ability to follow strict protocols and work in a regulated environment.
•	Strong teamwork and communication skills. 


Applications open on 2 July 2026 and close on 1 August 2026

Please send your CV to info@businessnest.com.au. Please include the job role title in your email.

AUD $85,000–$90,000 per annum plus Superannuation, depending on skills and experience.

About us:
NVD Fresh Produce Pty Ltd is a family-owned agricultural enterprise based in Walkaway, Western Australia, approximately 30 minutes from Geraldton. We operate approximately 4.2 hectares of plastic greenhouses in Walkaway and an additional 2 hectares of plastic greenhouses at the family’s original farm.

We are currently expanding our operations, having purchased 60 acres of land near Walkaway to support future growth and long-term sustainability. NVD Fresh Produce specialises in intensive greenhouse cultivation and is progressively diversifying its crop range, recognising crop rotation as a key strategy to preserve soil health, improve productivity, and maintain consistent supply.
The business is focused on strengthening its production capacity, improving operational systems and water management practices, and establishing a scalable and sustainable structure to support ongoing expansion within Western Australia’s fresh produce market.

The successful applicant will play an important role in supporting the continued growth and success of NVD Fresh Produce's farming operations.

Position Summary
The Horticulture Grower is responsible for planning, coordinating and carrying out vegetable crop production activities across NVD Fresh Produce's greenhouse and farming operations. The role supports efficient and sustainable crop production by managing crop establishment, cultivation, irrigation, fertiliser application, pest and disease control, harvesting activities, and maintaining high standards of crop quality, productivity and workplace safety.

Key Responsibilities
Crop Production Planning
•	Plan and coordinate vegetable crop production from soil preparation through to harvesting, taking into account production requirements and seasonal conditions. 
•	Select seeds, seedlings and planting materials and oversee crop establishment. 
Crop Management
•	Maintain crop production through cultivation, pruning, irrigation, fertiliser application and crop nutrition programs. 
•	Monitor crop health and implement pest, disease and weed management strategies to optimise crop quality and yield. 
Harvesting and Production Operations
•	Organise harvesting, grading, storage and packaging activities. 
•	Assist in coordinating the storage, grading, packaging and dispatch of fresh produce.
•	Monitor production schedules to meet customer and market requirements. 
•	Assist in achieving production targets to meet customer requirements and market demand.
Farm Operations
•	Assist in maintaining farm buildings, fencing, irrigation systems, equipment and water supply infrastructure.
•	Maintain production records and monitor crop performance. 
•	Support planning activities to improve production efficiency and sustainability. 
Workplace Safety and Team Support
•	Comply with workplace health and safety requirements. 
•	Assist in training and supporting farm employees where required. 
•	Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives across farming operations.

Qualifications and Skills
Applicants should possess one of the following:
•	A relevant AQF Certificate III or Certificate IV qualification (or equivalent); or 
•	At least 3 years' relevant employment experience in commercial horticultural production together with relevant formal training; or 
•	At least 5 years' relevant employment experience in commercial horticultural production where no relevant formal training is held.
In addition, applicants should demonstrate:
•	Knowledge of vegetable production, irrigation, fertiliser application, pest, disease and weed management. 
•	Ability to work effectively in a commercial horticultural production environment. 
•	Ability to follow work instructions and communicate effectively with supervisors and team members. 
•	Ability to work cooperatively as part of a team. 
•	Current driver's licence or the ability to obtain one will be highly regarded. 
•	Commitment to workplace health and safety

Support Worker 

Empowering People In Communities (EPIC) is a not-for-profit organisation that offers disability support and community services in the Pilbara and Goldfields.
Our aim is to empower clients through a range of services that support many people to live a more connected life through community.

Location: 
Karratha

Opportunity:
We’re seeking dedicated and compassionate Full Time Support Workers who are looking to challenge themselves and build on their skills and knowledge. We are seeking candidates who have a strong focus on personal care with flexible availability to cover a variety of shifts including but not limited to overnight shifts. This role provides a variety of support services including personal care, domestic and lifestyle support, and community inclusion, all guided by the participant’s individual NDIS support plan.

Duties and Responsibilities:
- Provide high-quality support that enhances independence, encourages participation, and aligns with individual goals.
- Deliver culturally appropriate support that respects the diversity of participants.
- Take direction from the person being supported, their family, and EPIC’s Client Coordinator.
- Maintain professionalism and positive relationships with clients, families, and colleagues.
- Accurately complete documentation, including case notes and incident reports, using EPIC’s systems.
- Assist with personal care and daily living tasks, particularly during night-time hours.
- Perform other duties as required by your manager.

Essential
- Current First Aid Certificate (or ability to obtain within three months)
- NDIS Worker Screening Check (or ability to obtain)
- WA “C” class driver’s licence (or overseas equivalent with valid temporary visa)
- Working with Children Check (mandatory)
- Availability for night shifts and sleepovers
- Demonstrated respect for people with disability and commitment to inclusion
- Ability to maintain confidentiality and communicate effectively
- Experience using digital rostering systems
- Willingness to work across a variety of shifts, including weekends and after-hours

Desirable  
- Previous experience providing personal care
- Experience supporting people with disability (formally or informally)
- Experience working with children
- Complex care experience (e.g. PEG feeding, fluids, puree diets)
- Manual handling experience or qualification
- Knowledge of NDIS Quality and Safeguards
- Certificate IV in Disability or Community Services

Why join the EPIC Team?
- Above Award Rates
- Salary Sacrifice up to $15,900 per annum
- Additional leave after 12 months service (part-time only)
- Quarterly bonus scheme
- Employee Assistance Program
- Training opportunities
- Corporate Health Insurance Discounts
- Access to discounts at over 9,000 retail locations across Australia

Shortlisting and interviews may commence as applications are received. EPIC reserves the right to close the advertisement early if a suitable candidate is identified.

To access the full Position Description or for further questions, please contact hr@empoweringpeople.org.au

EPIC is an Equal Employment Opportunity employer and values diversity and inclusion. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds. Due to the nature of participant preferences and support needs, female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply for this role. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people are encouraged to apply.

Water & the Environment are hot topics in Australia…			
Be part of a company that’s in the action!

Integra Water Treatment Solutions is a national, Australian owned company who specialize in commercial and industrial water treatment.  Our company has grown from humble beginnings in 1990 to now including 200 plus in our team Australia wide. Our Sydney operation is currently seeking expand the team with a motivated and enthusiastic person to be included our small but experienced team, specialising in water & wastewater treatment, reuse and environmental treatment systems & applications.  

Integra offer expertise in the following areas:
•	Cooling water treatment and tower cleaning
•	Boiler water treatment
•	Pre-treatment, filtration and desalination
•	Waste water treatment
•	Equipment design, repair and installation
•	Cleaning and hygiene solutions


Water & Wastewater Operations: Environmental Consultant 
To be successful in this role you will have experience in working in a team, have good interpersonal and communication skills and be self-motivated. You will have had experience with meeting scheduled customer wastewater service requirements and co-ordinating multiple and competing requirements to limited time frames.

Role Description:
•	Designing strategic environmental action plans to guide sustainable water and wastewater management across Integra Water's industrial, commercial and manufacturing client sites, identifying immediate priorities and establishing long-term treatment and compliance objectives. 
•	Monitoring compliance with environmental statutes and discharge regulations governing water treatment, effluent release and re-use, and initiating corrective measures to protect waterways and surrounding ecosystems. 
•	Conducting comprehensive site assessments prior to the installation or upgrade of water treatment, filtration and wastewater infrastructure to anticipate ecological and regulatory consequences. 
•	Recommending mitigation strategies to offset the environmental impact of industrial water use and effluent discharge, and to support restoration of affected water systems. 
•	Investigating how variables such as water chemistry, temperature, flow conditions, seasonal patterns and site-specific operational processes influence treatment performance and environmental outcomes. 
•	Collecting and interpreting data from water, effluent and soil analyses to evaluate contamination levels and inform treatment, filtration and re-use strategies. 
•	Developing environmental management policies and pollution control benchmarks for industrial and commercial water and wastewater operations, including standards for the treatment of disturbed or contaminated sites. 
•	Coordinating environmental initiatives across client facilities — including manufacturing plants, food processors and commercial premises — to protect water quality and support sustainable resource use. 
•	Compiling environmental data and technical resource inventories to support Integra Water's clients in land-use, treatment infrastructure and resource management decisions.

Requirements: 
•	Relevant Qualification
•	At least 3 years of experience
•	Strong understanding of water and wastewater treatment processes, data evaluation and compliance
•	Effective communicator, able to engage with clients and internal stakeholders across technical and non-technical levels
•	Ability to work effectively with a well-established management team 
•	Handle challenging situations

Position: Full Time (at least 38 hours per week)

Salary: $70,000 – 85,000 per year 

Working location: Miranda NSW 2228

Integra values hinge on our commitment to our customers, our solutions and most importantly, our commitment to our people.  We have a culture that encourages our people to make their positions with us their future careers.  Apply today if you feel you have what it takes to become a part of our unique team.  Further information on our company may be obtained at www.integrawater.com.au

All applications will be dealt with confidentially.  
Get Your Visa posted on behalf of Integra Water

Expected Salary: $72,000 – $82,000 per year

About Us:
We are a well-established landscaping and strata gardening company delivering high-quality outdoor maintenance and landscaping solutions across residential, strata, and commercial properties in Sydney. We pride ourselves on professional standards, reliability, and long-term client relationships, supported by a skilled and dedicated team.

Due to continued business growth, we are seeking an experienced Landscape Gardener to join our operations on a full-time basis.

About the Role
This role is responsible for the construction, maintenance, and ongoing care of landscaped areas across strata and commercial sites. You will work across multiple locations, delivering high- quality landscaping outcomes while ensuring safety, efficiency, and client satisfaction. This is a hands-on role suited to someone with solid horticultural knowledge, practical landscaping experience, and the ability to work independently while meeting quality and safety standards.

Key Responsibilities
Interpret landscape plans and site requirements for strata and commercial properties
Prepare landscaped areas including soil preparation, planting, turfing, and mulching
Select appropriate plants and materials based on site conditions and design intent
Install, test, maintain, and troubleshoot irrigation systems
Perform professional pruning, hedging, fertilisation, and plant health management
Maintain landscaped areas to a high standard across multiple sites
Identify pests, diseases, and landscape issues and apply appropriate treatments
Ensure all work complies with WHS regulations, environmental guidelines, and company procedures
Liaise with strata managers and internal teams regarding scheduled landscaping works
Ensure sites are maintained to company and client standards
Report any site issues or maintenance needs
Support team members and attend scheduled team meetings

Skills & Experience
Minimum 1 years experience as a Landscape Gardener, Gardener or in commercial landscaping
Strong knowledge of plants, turf management, irrigation systems, and soil preparation
Ability to read and implement landscape plans
Experience working across strata or multi-site environments
Good time management and organisational skills
Ability to work independently and as part of a team
Good communication skills for client and stakeholder interaction
Current Australian driver’s licence
Hold a Construction Induction Safety certificate (White Card)
Certificate III or higher in Landscape Construction, Horticulture, or a related field (desirable)

What We Offer
Full-time, ongoing employment
Stable workload across established client sites
Supportive team environment
Opportunity to grow with a well-regarded strata landscaping business

If you are an experienced Landscape Gardener who takes pride in delivering high-quality outdoor environments and enjoys working within a professional and supportive team, we would love to hear from you.

To apply, please follow the prompts and submit your resume. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Join Clean Green Strata and be part of a team committed to maintaining and enhancing outdoor spaces across Sydney.

Employer questions
Your application will include the following questions:
How many years' experience do you have in a Landscaping Role?
Which of the following statements best describes your right to work in Australia?
How many years' experience do you have as a Landscape Gardener?
Do you have a current Australian driver's licence?
Do you hold a Construction Induction Safety certificate (White Card)?
Have you completed a qualification in horticulture?
Do you have experience as an area or multi-site manager?

Graduate Accountant
Specialised Breeders Australia Pty Ltd
Bagshot, Victoria  |  Full-Time  |  $79,423 – $90,000 per annum
About Us
Specialised Breeders Australia Pty Ltd is a leading name in the poultry breeding industry, committed to operational excellence and sustainable production. We are seeking a motivated Graduate Accountant to join our finance team and support the financial operations of our growing business.
This is an excellent opportunity for accounting professional to gain broad exposure to financial and management accounting within a dynamic agribusiness environment, while working closely with senior finance leadership including the Financial Accountant, Management Accountant, Purchasing supervisor and CFO. 
About the Role
Reporting to the Financial Accountant, the Graduate Accountant will play a key role in accounts processing, statutory compliance, cost analysis and month-end reporting. This role offers genuine variety and the chance to build a strong foundation across all areas of financial accounting.
Key Duties and Responsibilities
•	Preparing and lodging monthly Business Activity Statements (BAS) and PAYG obligations in compliance with ATO requirements.
•	Preparing and submitting Chick Hatching and Egg Promotion Levy Returns in accordance with DAFF requirements and maintaining supporting accounting records.
•	Processing supplier invoices, creditor payments and foreign currency transactions through the ERP and banking systems.
•	Allocating and reconciling daily customer receipts and investigating payment discrepancies as they arise.
•	Undertaking company banking, monthly bank reconciliations and supporting schedules for financial reporting.
•	Preparing monthly and quarterly costing and variance reports for biological assets, production inputs, labour hire, utilities and operational expenses.
•	Assisting with month-end accounting, accruals, fixed asset register maintenance and audit support (interim and year-end).
•	Preparing employee-related statutory schedules, including PAYG withholding, Payroll Tax, Superannuation, Child Support and FBT obligations.
•	Maintaining and improving ERP accounting processes, internal controls and financial record-keeping systems.
•	Liaising with external stakeholders, including auditors, financial institutions and taxation authorities, as well as internal managers and stakeholders.
•	Coordinating with purchasing coordinators and operations managers to prepare monthly creditor and electricity accrual journals for review by the Financial Accountant.
•	Monitoring and analysing biological asset operating costs, expenditure trends and profitability, and reporting findings for month-end financial reporting.
•	Supporting the Financial Accountant with fixed asset additions, disposals and reconciliations, along with other ad-hoc accounting duties.
•	Providing financial and accounting support to managers and stakeholders, including advice on accounting procedures, cost control and reporting requirements.
•	Attending to general finance administration and responding to finance-related enquiries from internal stakeholders.
Qualifications and Experience
•	Minimum Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a closely related discipline.
•	Minimum two (2) year of relevant professional accounting experience.
•	Sound knowledge of accounting principles, financial reporting and taxation compliance.
•	Strong analytical, organisational and communication skills.
•	Working towards CA/CPA qualification is preferred. 
What We Offer
•	Competitive salary of $79,423– $90,000 per annum.
•	Mentoring and support provided towards CA/CPA qualification
•	Opportunity to gain exposure across other areas of the finance function.
•	Supportive team environment within a well-established agribusiness.
How to Apply
Click Apply Now to submit your resume and a cover letter outlining your suitability for the role.
Specialised Breeders Australia Pty Ltd is an equal opportunity employer.
